question: If tan A + sec A = 3, find tan A.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If sec A + tan A = x, then sec A − tan A = 1 / x.

Subtracting the two equations, we get: 2 tan A = x − (1 / x).

Given sec A + tan A = 3, so x = 3.

⇒ 2 tan A = 3 − (1 / 3) = 8 / 3

⇒ tan A = 4 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 4/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ sec A + tan A = 3

**Formula Used:**

⇒ sec A = 1 / cos A

⇒ tan A = sin A / cos A

⇒ sin² A + cos² A = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1 / cos A) + (sin A / cos A) = 3

⇒ (1 + sin A) / cos A = 3

Squaring both sides:

⇒ (1 + sin A)² / cos² A = 9

⇒ (1 + sin A)² / (1 − sin² A) = 9

⇒ (1 + sin A)² / [(1 − sin A) × (1 + sin A)] = 9

⇒ (1 + sin A) / (1 − sin A) = 9

⇒ 1 + sin A = 9 − 9 sin A

⇒ 10 sin A = 8

⇒ sin A = 8 / 10 = 4 / 5

⇒ In a right-angled triangle, sin A = Opposite / Hypotenuse = 4 / 5

⇒ Opposite = 4, Hypotenuse = 5

⇒ Adjacent = √(5² − 4²) = √(25 − 16) = √9 = 3

⇒ tan A = Opposite / Adjacent = 4 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 4/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Trigonometric Identities

⇒ sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 | sec² θ − tan² θ = 1 | cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1

Reciprocal Pair Logic

Since sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, the expressions (sec θ + tan θ) and (sec θ − tan θ) are always reciprocals of each other.

Cosecant and Cotangent Property

Similarly, if cosec θ + cot θ = x, then cosec θ − cot θ = 1 / x.

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of integers satisfying a² + b² = c² commonly used in trigonometry include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17).
